note: Printed claims only (Step 6). Wire list image-read at 400 dpi from BK6 printed p.59 (PDF p.65): 41 wires, matching programs.json wiresPrinted line for line; the [unverified] 3C/4C line flag (OCR 3C/AC) is settled, the image reads 3C/4C. No erratum names p.59 (errata.pdf PDF p.4 Book VI entries cover pp.51, 52, 53, 55, 57, 60 only), so errata_applied is empty and wires = as_printed. Fixture tier A: the circuit is combinational (lamp state is a function of the held buttons only; no hold path) and the motor and dial are unwired; release steps are untagged because no release is load-bearing (with every release deleted the six expects still pass). The circuit has no hold path (every coil is driven from a player-2 pushbutton N.O. contact, every lamp from a player-1 pushbutton through a relay contact), so a result shows only while both buttons are down; the script reads the printed To Play paragraph (Player 1 should move just before player 2 moves since the relays will move after player 2 indicates his move) as player 1 pressing and holding, player 2 pressing 100 ms later, the assertion taken with both held, then player 2 releasing, then player 1. Hold time, the 100 ms gap and the release order are not source timing. All nine move pairs are played. Asserted (six): each distinct-move pair against its printed rule and printed outcome line, light 1 on when player 1 wins and light 6 on when player 2 wins; the move-to-button mapping is the printed control table. Not asserted: the three same-move games (pb1/pb4, pb2/pb5, pb3/pb6). The page prints Tie: lights 3 and 4 come on but never states that equal moves are a tie; reading them as ties is an inference, so they are left to Step 7 (the simulator lights lamps 3 and 4 in all three). Also not asserted (derived, Step 7): which lamps stay off in each outcome, relay and indicator-lamp states, that nothing moves before player 2 pushes, and the state after release. The programs.json printedUnprinted text (Which move pairs win is not printed) is contradicted by the page, which prints all three rules.
